claims.problem: Adobe Flash Player was deprecated, breaking legacy games (Gunny, DDTank) and interactive SWF media on modern browsers without insecure desktop plugins.
claims.primary_user: Retro web gamers, Gunny / DDTank community players, Flash game archivists and web developers.
claims.why_now: Modern WebAssembly (Ruffle) combined with local WebSocket-to-TCP network bridging and Host-based path reverse proxying enables pure in-browser multiplayer Flash gameplay at 60 FPS without external desktop launchers.
claims.input: SWF files, Flashvars parameters, live game URLs (Zing Gunny, 123gn.net private server, DDTank custom servers), custom TCP socket host/port coordinates.
claims.core_transformation: Compiles and runs ActionScript 2/3 in WASM/WebGL; bridges raw TCP socket packets over WebSockets; proxies and rewrites cross-origin configuration while preserving pristine ZLIB binary streams.
claims.output: Smooth 60 FPS WebGL game viewport with full Vietnamese Unicode fonts, responsive gaming keyboard controls, live TCP multiplayer interaction, and comprehensive status monitoring.
claims.desired_outcome: Zero-friction, 1-click sync and gameplay for any Gunny server (official or private) directly inside modern browsers with premium glassmorphism dark UI.
claims.success: 100% verified gameplay on Zing Server 737 and 123gn.net private server, 60 FPS rendering, clear Vietnamese typography, and full Agent OS integrity compliance.
claims.acceptance_evidence: Zing Server 737 tutorial battle verified, 123gn.net private server full login & mail/guild loaded at 60 FPS, zero build errors.
claims.failure_conditions: Black screen rendering, binary corruption of compressed game XMLs, unmapped socket proxy ports, or browser window hijacking.
claims.scope: Frontend Ruffle WASM integration, Node.js Universal Bridge, Dynamic Reverse Proxy, Session Synchronization, Game Presets, Gaming Controls.
claims.non_goals: Modifying server-side backend logic, altering remote game databases, or creating unofficial game server emulators.
invariants: Preserve Agent OS ownership boundaries, keep binary game assets untouched, never alter client global configs, maintain reversible code changes.
constraints: Modern web browser with WebAssembly and WebGL2 support; Node.js runtime for bridge server; local ports 5173, 8080, 8081.
